ask: Which of my hooks exist only to make sessions remember things, and which could filing-at-once replace?
note: Audit done (Oct 26, read main b1e5a6d): plans/o5b-memory-hooks-audit.md. No hook exists only to make sessions remember something filing at once replaces; ruling_home and feedback_gate are filing at once's only enforcement, and the handoff hooks carry in-flight state no file holds. Deferred (shiv's decision): re-point feedback_gate task and ruling homes to tracked files, then trim the handoff's rulings sections.
title: Which hooks exist only to make sessions remember, and can filing at once retire them
why: Guards that make a session remember are a backstop. What actually works: anything that matters goes to a lasting home (a repo file, a roadmap page) in the same turn it's said. A session's job is filing, not remembering, so a compaction or a lost session costs nothing. This includes fb: items: tasks and ideas land in the repo's todo, not only the handoff, and each closed item is checked against its home.
